qa_pairs.question: I dropped a course after the census date this term. Will any of its tuition be reversed?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. Tuition for a course dropped after the standard add/drop period and after census is not reversed: 100% is reversed for a drop by the end of standard add/drop, 50% is reversed from the day after standard add/drop through the census date, and after census no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

contexts.text: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

qa_pairs.question: What must a student do to register for a course whose prerequisite they are currently taking?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A student currently taking a prerequisite may conditionally register for the next course, but the registration is removed if the prerequisite is not passed. Instructor permission alone does not replace a prerequisite unless the programme director also records the waiver.

contexts.text: A student currently taking a prerequisite may conditionally register for the next course, but the registration is removed if the prerequisite is not passed.

qa_pairs.expected_answer: Three consecutive unexplained absences trigger an academic-support alert; the alert itself is not a disciplinary finding. Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance.

contexts.text: Three consecutive unexplained absences trigger an academic-support alert; the alert itself is not a disciplinary finding.

qa_pairs.question: I want to withdraw from all my courses this term. What should I consider before doing so?

International students must consult the International Student Office before reducing their registered load.

qa_pairs.question: How must an excused absence be documented, and what does an excuse allow?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An absence is excused only after the student submits acceptable documentation through the portal within five business days of returning. An excused absence allows a reasonable alternative for participation work, but it does not automatically cancel a learning outcome or guarantee the same assessment format.

qa_pairs.question: I disagree with a final grade. What are the first steps in the grade appeal process?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A grade appeal is different from a service complaint. The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

contexts.text: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published.

A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination.
Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

qa_pairs.question: A student discussed a late add in July 2026 but submits the request on September 10, 2026, which is before the census date. Which registration policy version applies, and what does it require?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Version 2.0 applies because the late-add request is made on or after August 1, 2026, even if the student first discussed the request in July. Version 2.0 allows late adds only through the census date and charges USD 40 per course; a late add also requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of the USD 40 late-add fee within two business days of approval.

contexts.text: Registration Policy version 1.0, effective before August 1, 2026, allowed late adds for seven calendar days after standard add/drop and charged USD 25. Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.

Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date. A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval.

qa_pairs.question: A Merit Scholarship recipient missed one renewal requirement this term. What happens, and what would a second consecutive failed review do?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A first failure to meet one academic renewal requirement normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss, and during probation the award remains active. A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term. A serious-conduct sanction may end the award immediately and is not protected by the academic probation rule.

contexts.text: A first failure to meet one academic renewal requirement normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss. During probation, the award remains active.
A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term.
A serious-conduct sanction may end the award immediately and is not protected by the academic probation rule.

qa_pairs.question: Can a student receive an incomplete grade if they have completed only 60% of the assessed work of a course?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. An incomplete grade may be granted only when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently. The student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan, and the default deadline is the end of the next regular term; if no grade is submitted by that deadline, the I converts to F unless an approved extension exists.

contexts.text: An `I` incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently.

The student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan. The default deadline is the end of the next regular term. If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.
